AI Agents weren't collaborative. So we fixed it.
Cluing Hosted Agents are now live:
• Fully virtually hosted agents - not a local harness, a hosted agent
• Evolving skills - skills that live on real data and update as you learn
• Hosting built-In - publish apps, websites, dashboards
• One workspace for both people and agents - create agents, assign them tasks, and build knowledge as a team
Think Claude Code, but collaborative and with a setup so simple you can create agents and assign them tasks straight from your phone.
That's what we've built with Cluing 💛
Here's how it works:
1. Create your Agent - Head to the Agents tab, click + New Agent, give it a name, and write the ground-rule instructions it should follow for every task it takes on. [...] 2. Brief it with a Task - Every task is the specific job for that Agent: a name and a detailed description of what done looks like. The more detail you give, the better the result.
3. Feed it your knowledge - Ask for a topic to be included or build a connector to any app where your knowledge lives. Now the Agent works from real context instead of starting from zero.
4. Give it an assignment or let it run on its own schedule - You can switch to Autonomous and set a daily, weekly, or monthly routine for recurring work like research digests or reports.
5. Hand it off and collaborate - Reassign a Task's Owner to a teammate anytime, so the whole team can drive, monitor, and build on the same Agent's work.
True collaboration. [...] ##### Transcript

### Step 1 — Build the local shape of a hosted agent

A hosted agent isn’t a special framework or a special class. It’s an ordinary agent with one extra ingredient: a tiny hosting adapter that exposes it over HTTP using the OpenAI Responses protocol (note: this is independent from the model the agent uses internally, which can be any LLM from any provider) on port 8088.

The adapter is the contract between your code and Foundry’s runtime. As long as your container speaks the Responses protocol on 8088, Foundry doesn’t care what’s inside — MAF, LangGraph, pure LLM API calls, anything. That’s what makes Hosted Agents portable.

That’s what make your agent “hostable” in Foundry — all the rest remain untouched. [...] For a step by step tutorial, you can follow the official documentation here: Deploy a hosted agent — Microsoft Foundry | Microsoft Learn.

# What are hosted agents?

When you build agentic applications by using open-source frameworks, you typically manage many cross-cutting concerns: containerization, web server setup, security, memory persistence, scaling, instrumentation, and version rollbacks. These tasks become even more challenging in heterogeneous cloud environments.

Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service solve these challenges for Microsoft Foundry users. Hosted agents call models from the Foundry model catalog to perform reasoning while your custom code handles orchestration. By using this managed platform, you can deploy and operate AI agents securely and at scale. You can use your custom agent code or a preferred agent framework with streamlined deployment and management.

# What are hosted agents? [...] ## Key concepts

### Hosted agents

Hosted agents are containerized agentic AI applications that run on Agent Service. Unlike prompt-based agents—which are defined entirely through prompts and tool configuration in the Foundry portal—Hosted agents are your own code packaged as a container image. You choose the framework, control the runtime behavior, and deploy the image to Microsoft-managed infrastructure.

The platform automatically manages the container lifecycle based on activity, provisioning resources when you create a version and deprovisioning when the idle timeout is reached.
